# Measuring the factory

**Outcome (draft, #8, shared with ch 10):** the run record shows each human touch with its reason, and the intervention rate is reported.

## The pattern
- Outcomes, not completion: green CI or a merged PR is completion. Each run states an `intended_outcome` as a checkable claim, graded later as achieved, not_achieved or unknown (standing rule, 2026-11-06).
- "if you fail to collect the data, you can never measure the data". Collect telemetry and trajectory from the first run (05).
- "there should be multiple measurements, along with a testing harness that shows when results start trending good or bad… so you can make informed decisions on the data!" (02)
- Runtime metrics detect "when the agent goes off the rails". It "requires regular study. it's own OODA loop" (01).
- "repeating the same errors without taking those learnings back… hurts worse in terms of wasting tokens" (01). A prose prompt you can't trace or reproduce leaves nothing to measure against (01).
- Store what you can act on, not everything: keep parameter names, and parameter values only where analysis proves them valuable (05).
- Run records in two tiers, "like bronze/silver": the full redacted record in bronze until the retention policy, and a silver that is revised to keep the "proven" fields (05b, decision). Silver v1 is today's fields; promotion is decided by analysis "after we collect that data for a sprint or two" (05b).
- Retention is "up to each org". The book gives the pattern, not a number (05b).
- Tag every run's cost four ways (repo, issue, epic, requester), "that way you can attribute the cost at any level" (08). Compare GitHub, which bills one party per cost.
- Estimates turn caps into a forecast you can grade against actuals (05).
- From Cortex, unverified, not Shannon's words: capture the baseline before a change, measure per member rather than a fleet mean, and grade evidence as measured, replayed, estimated or hypothesis (02). `[VERIFY]` before using.

## How I set it up
- Interventions are recorded with a cause class (capability, skill, routing, quality, speed, policy) (standing rule, 2026-09-30). This is the measurement behind "the Hermes decline" in ToC v2.
- Retention is unset today, so bronze is kept forever. "we should probably lower that to a year at some point" (05b). An honest "what I gave up".

## What I use it for
- The Forgejo volume trend, with all its caveats (`vault: ideas/book-evidence-2026-11` §2). Use it as the trend after the method was applied, not head-to-head with the Databricks numbers.
